description: The exec plugin built into dprint, which formats files with external commands.

lineWidth.description: The width of a line the formatter will try to stay under. Available to commands as {{line_width}}.

indentWidth.description: The number of spaces for an indent. Available to commands as {{indent_width}}.

useTabs.description: Whether to use tabs (true) or spaces (false). Available to commands as {{use_tabs}}.

cacheKey.description: Change this to invalidate the incremental cache, ex. when a command's version changes.

cwd.description: The working directory to run the commands in. Defaults to the current working directory.

timeout.description: Seconds a command may take to format a file before it's killed and the format fails.

setupTimeout.description: Seconds a setup command may run before it's killed. A setup command that times out isn't run again for the other files.

playWithFire.description: Allows the exec commands of remote configuration (ex. an `extends` url) to run. `true` allows any program, or list the programs their commands and setup commands may run. Only a local configuration file can allow it.

items.$comment: A command needs a non-empty exts, fileNames or associations. Each alternative allows other properties, as tombi's strict mode otherwise treats it as allowing none.

command.description: The command to format with: the program and its arguments. The file text is passed to it on stdin and the formatted text is read from its stdout. Arguments may use {{file_path}}, {{line_width}}, {{use_tabs}}, {{indent_width}}, {{cwd}} and {{timeout}}.

exts.description: File extensions to format with this command.

fileNames.description: File names to format with this command, ex. for files without an extension.

associations.description: A glob of the file paths to format with this command. Prefer "exts" when possible.

stdin.description: Whether to pass the file text to the command on stdin.

cwd.description: The working directory to run this command in.

cacheKeyFiles.description: Files whose contents invalidate the incremental cache when they change, ex. the command's own configuration file.

setupCommand.description: A command to run once before this command formats its first file, ex. to install it. It's killed after "setupTimeout" seconds.
